speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned experiencing intense itching and developing red bumps on your thigh and elsewhere; can you tell me how long you have had these symptoms and if they are spreading?

speaker: Patient
text: 47-year-old male. The patient presents with intense itching of his right thigh region for the past few days. He also mentions the recent formation of ‘red bumps’ in the same area. The patient has recently attended a business conference in Miami. He has a past medical history of hypertension, diabetes type 2, and hyperlipidemia. The patient’s medication regimen includes enalapril, metformin, and atorvastatin. He denies any history of smoking or drinking.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Scabies infestation.

The onset of intense itching and red bumps shortly after attending a conference in Miami is highly suggestive of scabies, a contagious skin infestation. Given your history of diabetes and hypertension, I would also like to rule out a drug eruption from your current medications or secondary bacterial infection. Have you noticed any burrow-like tracks between your fingers, on your wrists, or around your waistline?
